src: ; 15 mandelbrot — the Mandelbrot set: beautiful, and the textbook case of divergence
; Each pixel is a complex number c. Iterate z = z*z + c from z = 0 and count
; the steps until |z| > 2 (it "escapes"). Points that never escape are in the
; set (black); the rest are colored by how fast they escaped.
; Every lane iterates a DIFFERENT number of times. A warp keeps issuing the
; loop until its slowest lane is done, with the finished lanes idle. Along the
; edge of the set, neighbouring pixels differ wildly, so SIMD efficiency drops.
; (Try the "Pixels and warps" lab to see how warp shape changes this.)
; Arithmetic is Q16.16 fixed point: 1.0 = 65536, QMUL = (a * b) >> 16.
; The image is 32 x 16 pixels covering x in [-2.5, 1.5], y in [-1, 1].
;   __global__ void mandel(uint32_t* fb, float x0, float y0, float step, int maxit) {
;       float cx = x0 + threadIdx.x * step, cy = y0 + blockIdx.x * step;
;           float t = zx*zx - zy*zy + cx; zy = 2*zx*zy + cy; zx = t; it++;
.equ X0, STEP / 2 - 5 * ONE / 2      ; x of the first pixel center (-2.4375)
.equ Y0, STEP / 2 - ONE              ; y of the first pixel center (-0.9375)
MAD  R2, R0, R9, R2        ; cx = x0 + x * step
MAD  R3, R1, R9, R3        ; cy = y0 + y * step
SETP.GE P1, R6, R11        ; out of iterations?
@P0 BRA  done                  ; <- lanes leave the loop at different times
ADD  R5, R9, R3            ; zy = 2 zx zy + cy
ADD  R4, R4, R2            ; zx = zx^2 - zy^2 + cx
done:                          ; min-PC scheduling reconverges the warp here
MIN  R7, R7, R9            ; red   = min(255, 24 * it)
MAX  R12, R12, R13         ; blue  = max(0, 170 - 12 * it)
@P2 MOVI R7, 0                 ; never escaped: inside the set, black
ADD  R9, R9, R0            ; pixel index
